title: Computer Use Benchmark Task
description: A declarative macOS computer-use task. Tasks are data, never code: the runner executes the instruction through a real model host and judges success purely from the declared success_criteria (filesystem state, system defaults, HTTP fixture state, or human review). No per-task coordinates or hardcoded action sequences are allowed — a criterion must be satisfiable in multiple ways.

id.description: Globally unique kebab-case id (also the trace/result key).

apps_required.description: App bundle names that must be available (e.g. TextEdit, Finder, Safari).

scratch_required.description: true when the task uses the run's scratch directory ({{SCRATCH}} placeholder).

fixture_required.description: true when the task needs the local fixture web app ({{FIXTURE_URL}} placeholder).

initial_state.description: Path (relative to benchmarks/) to a script that prepares the task's initial state before the run; the instruction must describe the state the model will find.

instruction.description: The natural-language instruction handed to the model. Must not reference task ids, coordinates, or the success criteria.

contains.description: For file_contains/file_not_contains: the substring that must (not) appear in the file.

pattern.description: For dir_contains: glob pattern (e.g. 'Screenshot*') matched against directory entries.

defaults_expected.description: For defaults_matches: expected value (string or boolean).

task_key.description: For http_check: the fixture state key to query via /check?task=<task_key>.

reason.description: For human_review: what a human should verify (shown in the report).

cleanup_script.description: Path (relative to benchmarks/) to a script restoring the system after the task (e.g. revert system defaults). Runner executes it after each run when the run dir is not --keep-files.
